articles.title: Maro Itoje warns England not to sleepwalk into clash with Eddie Jones’s Japan
articles.summary: ‘Japan have a distinct way of playing,’ says captain. Steve Borthwick hails ‘weird and wonderful’ Jones. Maro Itoje has insisted England will be ready for any curveballs Eddie Jones may throw on Saturday, warning his side they cannot “sleepwalk” into battle against Japan.
body: Jones, England’s longest-serving head coach after his stint between 2015 and 2022, has strongly hinted he will set his side up to unsettle his former charges at Twickenham, warning that they do not like “unorthodox” rugby. The hosts are heavy favourites to back up last week’s record win over Australia with another emphatic victory and have never lost to Japan but Steve Borthwick has made 10 personnel and two positional changes, fielding an inexperienced side against that of his predecessor.

“The overarching message this week is that we need to be alive,” said Itoje. “It’s impossible to tick off every eventuality that an opposition might do, especially a team like Japan, who have a very distinct way of playing. They’re very consistent at getting speed into the game. They could do a number of things, so let’s be alive and let’s not sleepwalk into things and think ‘most teams play like this’ because Japan aren’t most teams.

articles.title: Arokodare double secures Nigeria win in Afcon 2027 qualifier
articles.summary: Tolu Arokodare scores twice in the second half as Nigeria claim a 3-1 win over Tanzania to bolster their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.
body: With the East Africans already assured of a spot at the finals, the Super Eagles are battling for the one qualification spot available in Group L and have little margin for error after losing 3-0 in Guinea-Bissau in September.
Alhassan Yusuf kept his composure to slot Nigeria into a second-minute lead in Uyo from Ademola Lookman's pass, but the visitors equalised through Alphonce Msanga just after the half-hour mark.
Arokodare climbed off the bench at half-time and cleverly flicked home Wilfred Ndidi's low ball to restore the lead for the West Africans in the 52nd minute.

And the Ajax striker, who is on a season-long loan from Wolves, gave the Super Eagles breathing space eight minutes later when he controlled Moses Usor's cross from the left and smashed in from 12 yards out.

articles.title: McGree helps Socceroos put drama behind them and leave Qatar reeling
articles.summary: Qatar 0-3 Australia (McGree 5, Yengi 32, Irankunda 40) Julen Lopetegui under pressure as Qatar head coach. It was a win almost as comfortable as the buildup had been turbulent, as the Socceroos placed the drama of a week dominated by talk of everything but the football aside and cruised to a…
body: Pressing high, Australia’s men were ruthless in attack and dominant whenever their opponents even thought about getting forward, putting the result beyond doubt inside the opening 45 minutes. It took until the 38th for Qatar to register a touch in the Australia penalty area, and by that point they were down 2-0, with the third added for good measure just two minutes later. When Almoez Ali registered the reigning Asian champions’ first shot in the 72nd minute, Tony Popovic had emptied his bench, and the debutant Sam Klein hurled himself in front of the attempt before Patrick Beach had to worry about making a save.

Almost all focus heading into Friday’s contest was elsewhere, placed on the continuing back-and-forth over the Socceroos’ clash with Jordan next Tuesday, with an announcement coming on Thursday that the game was being moved to Doha. Riley McGree’s first goal for the national team in more than four years only five minutes into the contest, then, almost felt like a signal they were ready to let their football do the talking.

articles.title: Tearful Pochettino says United job was ‘difficult to turn down’ in USMNT farewell
articles.summary: Coach was ‘transparent’ in dealings with club, federation. Pochettino had signed deal to stay with US through 2030. There were always going to be tears at Mauricio Pochettino’s news conference at US Soccer’s national training center on Friday. It was only a matter of when.
body: “I think [the decision was],” Pochettino said, pausing to compose himself, “one of the most difficult decisions of our careers. Thank you guys. Thank you so much.”

The news conference read very much as a farewell to Pochettino, but there is still work to be done. The Argentinian will guide the USMNT through a pair of Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday. In the meantime, the future United coach did his best to address questions about his departure and what comes next.

“These moments are not easy decisions,” a reflective Pochettino told the media. “Normally it’s the opposite. Normally you get sacked and you cry because you want to stay and you’re sacked by [the club]. It’s a tough decision but at the same time we are excited for the next step forward.”
Pochettino characterized United’s interest and negotiations as having come together at the last minute, essentially, with contact between the two sides first made Sunday.

articles.title: Estonia latest country to ban Russian athletes
articles.summary: Estonia is the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine.
body: The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus.

In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality".
They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military.
Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms.

articles.title: Beirne leads Ireland bid to build on strong start
articles.summary: Tadhg Beirne, so often Ireland's 'Mr Dependable', leads the team's bid to improve on last week's win over Argentina against Fiji on Saturday.
body: As Tadhg Beirne prepares to captain Ireland at home for the first time, it is worth recapping the impressive manner in which he has built up his CV in recent years.
Since missing the final three games of the Six Nations Grand Slam campaign in 2023 with an ankle injury, Beirne has missed just three Ireland Tests.
He was rested against Italy in 2024 and missed last year's summer meetings with Georgia and Portugal while on British and Irish Lions duty.
Such big-game ubiquity is not easily found in the modern game - and Beirne has often delivered in red and green.

articles.title: Riley determined to prove himself a world champion in waiting
articles.summary: Viddal Riley will put himself on a path to a cruiserweight world title shot, if he can defend the European championship against Seydi Coupe on Saturday.
body: Only 14 fights into his pro career, Riley is already rated as the IBF's No. 2 contender for their world championship.
The Londoner wants to showcase himself as a world champion in waiting against Coupe.
"I think I'm the most well-rounded cruiserweight in the world," Riley told Sky Sports.
"I think we've trained for that because we want to cover every aspect of the game. We don't want to be lacking any area when it comes to movement, speed, IQ. All these things, I have them."

articles.title: Eight sentenced to jail over Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl
articles.summary: Eight people face prison sentences for their part in mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.
body: A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slapping former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind.
Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams, with Abu Dhabi police later confirming the incident led to 10 arrests being made.
According to a social media post by Abu Dhabi's judicial department, all 10 defendants have been convicted for their part in the brawl.

A report by Abu Dhabi news outlet the National, external went into more detail, adding that six of the defendants were sentenced to six months in prison, fined £62,000 each and ordered to be deported after completing their sentences.

articles.title: England respond to Jones' mind games ahead of Japan match
articles.summary: England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand.
body: Jones is aiming to disrupt Steve Borthwick's side by hitting them with the unexpected in the belief they will be "a little bit distracted" by the All Blacks' visit to Allianz Stadium on November 21.
New Zealand are the box-office fixture of the campaign ahead of finals weekend but England deny they are looking beyond Japan.
"That's nowhere near the case because we understand how important this game is," scrum coach Tom Harrison said.
"We understand the challenge Japan can throw at us and we have to be alive in every single moment to the type of rugby they play.

articles.summary: An emotional Mauricio Pochettino said that leaving his role with the United States was the "toughest decision of his career" but admitted he couldn't turn down the chance to become head coach of Manchester United.
body: Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup.
The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti.
Speaking in his pre-match press conference before his penultimate game, Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision.
"In some part, this is a very sad decision. In another part, we are professionals. This is the next step to try and make your dreams come true," the former Spurs and Chelsea boss said.

articles.title: Jonbon records Shloer Chase hat-trick at Cheltenham
articles.summary: Harry Cobden made his first ride on Jonbon in public a successful one as the odds-on favourite landed a third Shloer Chase in gritty fashion at Cheltenham.
body: Never out of the first two in 29 races, Nicky Henderson's charge is approaching veteran status at the age of 10 and was winning for the 21st time in his stellar career.

His task was made easier with the late withdrawal of Gidleigh Park, but Mighty Bandit kept him honest after the last, with the 1-2 favourite pulling away again towards to line to win by two and a quarter lengths.
Cobden said: "I'm so fortunate to be in this position riding all of these great horses and there's so many in the camp to look forward to, you do have to pinch yourself a little bit.

"I was really looking forward to it and pressure is just something you put on yourself isn't it. There was no point having a sleepless night over a Shloer Chase though as what would I be like in March!"

articles.title: Cordell Volson, former Bengals offensive lineman, signs with Seahawks
articles.summary: Former Cincinnati Bengals offensive lineman Cordell Volson was signed to the Seattle Seahawks ' practice squad, the team announced. Volson reportedly tried out for the Dallas Cowboys in September. Volson was released by the Tennessee Titans in August.
body: Volson was injured during training camp with the Bengals in 2025 and missed the entire season. He signed in March with the Titans after becoming a free agent after the season.

Volson, who turned 28 in July, didn't miss a game during his first three seasons with the Bengals, starting 48 of the 50 games in which he played. He also played in three playoff games during Cincinnati's 2022 postseason.
The Bengals selected Volson, a former North Dakota State standout, in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft.

"If Cordell Volson ends up logging enough snaps for the Seahawks, this could be a good test to learn whether snap count boosts apply for compensatory free agents across multiple teams after being cut," Over The Cap contributor Nick Korte tweeted.

articles.title: One Stat That Explains Chelsea Woes This Season
articles.summary: Chelsea have been somewhat inconsistent this year despite occupying fifth place in the Premier League table. They’re out of the EFL Cup, they’ve had some high-scoring games, and they’re almost perfectly balanced in mediocrity, with five league wins and four league losses with 19 goals scored and 16…
body: In the league, the top five leaders in expected goals are as follows. Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, and Romeo Lavia. Yes, a defensive midfielder who has dealt with some minor injuries and missed games is the fifth-highest expected goalscorer for the Blues. If you’re not already amazed, let’s explain what this means.

As anyone who has watched the team knows, everything good that this team does flows through the front three. When this works, we see big wins like the Bournemouth 5-1, but when it doesn’t we get a 1-0 loss to Sunderland with a sub-1 xG generated against the bottom-placed team in the division. This also means that the squad aren’t making use of set pieces to generate chances for more physical defenders or from open play from the wing-backs. All the burden is on the attacking group with the occasional pop from midfield making up the rest of their goalscoring output.
